slides: Welcome back. Let's briefly recall when an answer cannot be determined. The next questions will use our other two tools.

slides.say: Remember the crates question. Knowing the combined weight didn't tell us each crate's weight. Different pairs could fit. We can use that idea to check whether an answer can be determined.
Suppose two a plus three p is thirteen. If a is two and p is three, we get four plus nine, thirteen. If a is five and p is one, we get ten plus three, thirteen too. Both pairs fit the given equation.
at: two a plus three p is thirteen
a is two and p is three
a is five and p is one

slides.say: Now they ask for three a plus two p. With the first pair, three times two is six, and two times three is six. Six plus six is twelve.

With the second pair, three times five is fifteen, and two times one is two. Fifteen plus two is seventeen. Both pairs fit the given, but they give different answers: twelve and seventeen. So the answer cannot be determined.
at: So the answer cannot be determined

slides.say: That's the check: two allowed cases give different results. Then there isn't one answer fixed by the givens. Let's see the other two tools in the questions. I'll see you in the next video.
